transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO, Pegasus), Devon Lee (ML Engineer), Priya Narayan (Security), Noah Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery for migrating Pegasus workloads from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated; focus on compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, eval parity, security (SOC2/KMS/SSO), and pilot/benchmark next steps.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, i'm Samira, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our SE. can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Marta: hi, i'm marta, cto at pegasus. we run customer-facing analytics chat and document search, currently on openai api with some internal vLLM experiments.
[00:22] Devon: devon here, ML eng, i manage the inference stack and ops for the models.
[00:28] Priya: priya, security lead, will be validating compliance and data flows.
[00:33] Liam: great, thanks. quick context question — what's driving the migration consideration? cost, latency, control?
[00:42] Noah: mostly cost and SLA predictability; also we want control over data residency and to reduce dependency on a single vendor.
[00:50] Marta: and evaluation parity. we have custom prompts that behave slightly different on our vllm local runs vs openai. we want to make sure any hosted/dedicated deployment gives the same model outputs.
[01:10] Samira: totally. for that, we typically run parity benchmarks — same prompts, same few-shot contexts, and compare tokens, probabilities and the top-n generations. we can run against our curated open models and also run a dedicated environment to validate determinism.
[01:28] Devon: question — how do you handle vllm/tgi compatibility? we currently use vllm for on-prem lower-latency inference and TGI for some experiments. will migrating to Redwood Dedicated break our tooling?
[01:40] Liam: short answer: we support standard model formats and most weights used by vllm/tgi. runtime differences can cause minor output drift, especially with quantization or kernel differences. we try to preserve eval parity by matching sampling parameters, tokenization, and using same model variant. there are sometimes differences due to optimized kernels or fp16 quantization.
[02:04] Priya: on security — do you offer private deployments with KMS and SOC2 logs?
[02:11] Samira: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated both support customer-managed KMS integrations (Cloud KMS/HSM), audit logs, RBAC and SSO (SAML/Okta). SOC2 attestation is available; we'll share the pack.
[02:25] Marta: good. also, our legal team asks about data retention and whether requests are stored in the hosted service.
[02:32] Liam: hosted API by default stores minimal telemetry and you can configure retention; Dedicated gives you isolation and you can opt for no retention. Private on-prem gives total control. we can detail retention policies in the security docs.
[02:45] Noah: for performance, we care about p50/p95 latency under our conversational load — about ~120 qps blended, 90% short prompts under 512 tokens, some long context work at 4k tokens. how does Dedicated sizing look?
[02:58] Liam: we'll propose GPU pool sizing based on peak concurrency and target latency. autoscaling and burst capacity are options. also batching and KV cache reduce token cost and improve throughput — we'll include recommended configs in the sizing.
[03:15] Devon: when you say 'kv cache' — is that compatible with our existing vllm cache patterns?
[03:22] Liam: conceptually yes; we expose prefix caching and token-level caching. implementation differs but we can simulate your workload in a benchmark to measure cache hit rates.
[03:30] Marta: on model parity — we ran tgi locally with 4-bit quantization and saw some hallucination delta versus openai. will your quantization profiles affect answer quality?
[03:41] Liam: potentially. we have quantization profiles tuned per model; our Optimize tooling recommends profiles that balance cost and quality. for the pilot we'll test your prompt set across the same quantization and kernel choices to see where drift appears.
[03:56] Priya: what about network egress and VPC peering for private? our infra team requires VPC peering and traffic through internal gateways.
[04:05] Samira: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link options; Private on-prem can be air-gapped. we'll note the network requirements for the pilot.
[04:16] Noah: competitor question — some folks mentioned Anthropic and Cohere. do you recommend any model choices for parity?
[04:24] Liam: we maintain a model catalog with Redwood-verified performance profiles. if you're currently on OpenAI's text-davinci style family, we'll map to an open checkpoint with similar tokenizer and sampling behavior. for Anthropic-like outputs we'd choose a different family. part of the discovery is matching the model family and sampling parameters.
[04:44] Devon: can you run a blind A/B eval with our current OpenAI outputs? we want to be sure users won't notice regressions.
[04:51] Samira: yes, we do blind A/B and MRR/QA metric comparisons. please share your prompt set and reference outputs; we'll run the parity eval and produce diffs and statistical significance.
[05:05] Marta: what's the timeline to pilot? we ideally want to start a 2-week pilot in late march.
[05:12] Samira: that should be fine. typical pilot flow: share prompts+data, agree success metrics, Redwood runs benchmark on Dedicated (or Private trial), then we evaluate and iterate.
[05:22] Priya: one compliance question — do you keep PII in logs during pilot? we need an option to scrub or to host the pilot in a Private environment.
[05:30] Liam: we can either scrub inputs, run on Dedicated with retention disabled, or run on your Private environment. we recommend starting Dedicated with retention disabled for speed, and if compliance requires, move to Private.
[05:42] Noah: tech detail — are there pre-built connectors to our feature store and vector DB? we use a hosted Milvus cluster and have embeddings in postgres.
[05:51] Liam: we have integrations and flexible SDKs; for vector DBs we'll point to ingestion best practices and can support a vector cache layer. we also expose embedding APIs so you can continue storing embeddings in postgres or milvus.
[06:05] Devon: what about model updates and rollouts — can we pin versions and do canary?
[06:12] Samira: yes, rollouts, A/B, canary, automatic fallback to cheaper variants are supported in the console. we'll show that in the demo.
[06:20] Marta: pricing concerns — our finance wants TCO vs OpenAI; can you provide committed pricing examples for Dedicated vs per-token hosted?
[06:28] Samira: yes, i'll send committed pricing scenarios with committed GPU months and expected break-even vs hosted.
[06:34] Noah: ok, next steps and owners?
[06:38] Samira: i'll summarize. action items we heard: send pricing and sizing, run parity benchmark, share security docs and SOC2, customer to share prompt set and sample anonymized data. we'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week.
[06:52] Marta: sounds good. one more question — our engineers use the vllm pipeline for streaming and low-latency callbacks, do you support streaming with token-level events?
[07:02] Liam: yes, streaming responses and function/tool calling are supported; callbacks can be wired similarly to your vllm event hooks.
[07:12] Priya: for SSO and RBAC, does Redwood integrate with SCIM?
[07:18] Samira: yes, SAML/SCIM and granular RBAC are available for Enterprise Dedicated/Private.
[07:25] Devon: curious — in our latency tests, TGI had slightly less jitter than vllm for short prompts; will that show up on Dedicated?
[07:33] Liam: jitter often depends on batching policies and GPU kernel scheduling. for Dedicated we can tune batching thresholds to minimize jitter at the cost of some throughput. we'll include that in the benchmark matrix.
[07:46] Noah: anything else?
[07:48] Samira: just to confirm owners and dates — samira pricing by 3/6, liam benchmark infra by 3/10, customer shares dataset by 3/8, deep dive 3/11.
[07:58] Marta: yep confirmed. thanks all.
[08:02] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and security docs.

(Transcript notes: occasional ASR mis-hearings: 'vllm' sometimes transcribed as 'VLM', 'TGI' as 't-g-i', 'KV cache' as 'k-v cache'. Some speaker labels were concise rather than full names. Natural pauses and crosstalk at 03:30 and 06:38.)

Topics covered:
- Migration drivers: cost, control, SLAs, data residency
- Compatibility: vLLM/TGI model format and runtime drift
- Eval parity: blind A/B tests, metrics, prompt set sharing
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SCIM, retention policies
- Deployment options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, VPC peering
- Performance: batching, KV cache, GPU sizing, latency vs throughput tradeoffs
- Next steps and ownership

Questions (auto):
1) Can Redwood match OpenAI outputs exactly? answer: often close but minor drift possible; parity testing recommended.
2) Is Dedicated compliant with our SSO/KMS requirements? answer: yes, with integrations; will supply docs.
3) How long to pilot? answer: 2 weeks typical for parity benchmark.

End of transcript.
